questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the "Right to Equality before Law" guaranteed?
questions.explanation: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution states that the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced the words "Socialist, Secular and Integrity" into the Preamble of India?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added three new words—Socialist, Secular and Integrity—to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency under Article 352?
questions.explanation: By the 44th Amendment Act, Articles 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offences) and 21 (protection of life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended during an emergency.

questions.question: Who described the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) as the "Heart and Soul of the Constitution"?
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) as the very heart and soul of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which writ is issued by courts to secure the release of a person unlawfully detained?
questions.explanation: Habeas Corpus literally means "to have the body of" and is issued to produce a detained person before the court to examine the legality of detention.

questions.question: “கற்க கசடறக் கற்பவை கற்றபின் நிற்க அதற்குத் தக” - இக்குறட்பாவில் பயின்று வந்துள்ள மோனை யாது?
questions.explanation: செய்யுளின் நான்கு சீர்களிலும் முதல் எழுத்து ஒன்றி வருவது "முற்று மோனை" எனப்படும் (கற்க, கசடறக், கற்பவை, கற்றபின்).

questions.question: ‘செங்கதிர்’ - பிரித்து எழுதுக:
questions.explanation: ஈறுபோதல் விதியின்படி செம்மை + கதிர் என்பது "செங்கதிர்" எனப் புணரும்.

questions.question: ‘ஒழுக்கமுடைமை’ அதிகாரம் திருக்குறளில் எந்தப் பாலில் அமைந்துள்ளது?
questions.explanation: ஒழுக்கமுடைமை அதிகாரம் அறத்துப்பாலில் இல்லறவியலில் 14-வது அதிகாரமாக அமைந்துள்ளது.

questions.question: பொருந்தாச் சொல்லைக் கண்டறிக:
questions.explanation: முதல் மூன்றும் திருக்குறளின் அதிகாரப் பெயர்கள்; மரூஉ என்பது இலக்கணச் சொல் வகை ஆகும்.

questions.question: “தமிழ்த்தாத்தா” என்று போற்றப்படும் தமிழ் அறிஞர் யார்?
questions.explanation: பழங்காலத் தமிழ் ஓலைச்சுவடிகளைத் தேடித் தொகுத்துப் பதிப்பித்த உ.வே. சாமிநாதையர் "தமிழ்த்தாத்தா" என அழைக்கப்படுகிறார்.

questions.explanation: The Sun is the star at the center of the Solar System and principal energy source.

questions.question: Which star is at the centre of our solar system?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the star at the centre of the solar system; the planets orbit it.

questions.question: Which planet is commonly called the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Iron-rich dust on Mars gives its surface a reddish appearance.

questions.question: What is the main cause of day and night on Earth?
questions.explanation: Earth rotates on its axis, bringing different regions into and out of sunlight.

questions.question: A light-year is a unit of measurement of what?
questions.explanation: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of length?
questions.explanation: The metre (m) is the SI base unit of length.

questions.question: Which instrument is commonly used to measure electric current?
questions.explanation: An ammeter measures electric current and is connected in series in a circuit.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.question: Which of the following is a derived SI unit?
questions.explanation: The joule is a derived unit of energy, equivalent to newton metre.

questions.question: Which quantity is calculated by dividing distance travelled by time taken?
questions.explanation: Average speed equals total distance travelled divided by total time taken.

questions.question: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of:
questions.explanation: The first law describes the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion, called inertia.

questions.question: According to Newton's third law, action and reaction forces are:
questions.explanation: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction and act on different bodies.

questions.question: The SI unit of acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the change in velocity per unit time, measured in metres per second squared.

questions.question: Pressure is defined as:
questions.explanation: Pressure is the normal force acting per unit area.

questions.question: Which form of energy does a moving object possess?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses because of its motion.

questions.question: The SI unit of power is:
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy; its SI unit is the watt.

questions.question: A compressed spring stores mainly:
questions.explanation: When compressed, a spring stores elastic potential energy.

questions.topic: Everyday Applications of Basic Principles of Mechanics, Electricity, Magnetism, Light, Sound, Heat and Nuclear Physics
questions.question: A fuse in a household electrical circuit is used mainly to:
questions.explanation: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds a safe value.

questions.topic: Everyday Applications of Basic Principles of Mechanics, Electricity, Magnetism, Light, Sound, Heat and Nuclear Physics
questions.question: Which process transfers heat through a metal spoon placed in hot tea?
questions.explanation: Conduction transfers heat through a material by particle interactions.

questions.topic: Everyday Applications of Basic Principles of Mechanics, Electricity, Magnetism, Light, Sound, Heat and Nuclear Physics
questions.question: The bending of light when it passes from air into water is called:
questions.explanation: Refraction is the change in direction of light due to a change in its speed between media.

questions.topic: Everyday Applications of Basic Principles of Mechanics, Electricity, Magnetism, Light, Sound, Heat and Nuclear Physics
questions.question: Which device converts electrical energy into mechanical energy?
questions.explanation: An electric motor uses electrical energy to produce mechanical motion.

questions.topic: Everyday Applications of Basic Principles of Mechanics, Electricity, Magnetism, Light, Sound, Heat and Nuclear Physics
questions.question: The pitch of a sound mainly depends on its:
questions.explanation: Higher frequency is perceived as higher pitch.

questions.topic: Everyday Applications of Basic Principles of Mechanics, Electricity, Magnetism, Light, Sound, Heat and Nuclear Physics
questions.question: In a parallel household circuit, appliances are connected so that they:

options.text: All receive the same current only
Must all be switched on together

questions.explanation: Parallel branches provide separate paths, allowing appliances to work independently.

questions.question: Which of the following is an element?
questions.explanation: Oxygen contains only one kind of atom and is therefore an element.

questions.question: Water is classified as a compound because it:

options.text: Contains only one type of atom
Has hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined

questions.explanation: Water has hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined in a fixed proportion.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of common salt?
questions.explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride, with formula NaCl.

questions.question: Which method is suitable for separating an insoluble solid from a liquid?
questions.explanation: Filtration retains an insoluble solid while the liquid passes through the filter.

questions.question: Blue litmus paper turns red in:
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red.

questions.question: A solution with pH 7 at room temperature is generally:
questions.explanation: A pH of 7 is neutral at room temperature.

questions.question: The reaction between an acid and a base is called:
questions.explanation: Neutralisation produces salt and water in a typical acid-base reaction.

questions.question: Which substance is commonly used as an antacid?
questions.explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is a base that neutralises excess stomach acid.

questions.question: Petroleum is separated into useful fractions mainly by:
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation separates petroleum components according to their boiling ranges.

questions.question: Which petroleum fraction is commonly used as road surfacing material?
questions.explanation: Bitumen is a heavy petroleum fraction used in road construction.

questions.question: LPG used for domestic cooking mainly contains:
questions.explanation: Liquefied petroleum gas commonly consists mainly of propane and butane.

questions.question: Petroleum and natural gas are described as non-renewable because they:

options.text: Take millions of years to form

questions.explanation: Their formation takes geological timescales, so they cannot be replenished quickly.

questions.question: Which three elements are represented by NPK in fertilizers?
questions.explanation: NPK stands for nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, essential plant nutrients.

questions.question: Urea is an important source of:
questions.explanation: Urea is a nitrogen-rich chemical fertilizer.

questions.question: Which practice helps reduce excessive fertilizer runoff?

options.text: Applying fertilizer based on soil testing

questions.explanation: Soil testing helps determine crop nutrient needs and supports balanced application.

questions.question: Organic manure generally differs from chemical fertilizer because it:
questions.explanation: Organic manure contributes organic matter and can improve soil structure as well as supply nutrients.

questions.question: A herbicide is used to control:
questions.explanation: Herbicides are pesticides designed to control unwanted plants or weeds.

questions.question: Which is an example of biological pest control?

options.text: Releasing a natural predator of a pest

questions.explanation: Biological control uses natural enemies such as predators or parasites to reduce pest populations.

questions.question: Why should pesticide labels be followed carefully?

options.text: To ensure safe and correct use

questions.explanation: Labels provide directions on dosage, protective measures, storage and safe application.

questions.question: The unintended harmful effect of a pesticide on organisms other than the target pest is called:
questions.explanation: Pesticides can affect beneficial insects, wildlife and other non-target organisms.

questions.question: An ore is best described as:

options.text: A mineral from which a metal can be extracted economically

questions.explanation: An ore is a naturally occurring material from which a metal can be extracted profitably.

questions.question: Rusting of iron requires the presence of:
questions.explanation: Iron rusts in the presence of oxygen and water/moisture.

questions.question: Brass is an alloy mainly of:
questions.explanation: Brass is primarily made from copper and zinc.

questions.question: Galvanisation protects iron by coating it with:
questions.explanation: A zinc coating protects iron from corrosion.

questions.question: Adding water to milk is an example of:

options.text: A possible form of food adulteration

questions.explanation: Adding water can reduce the quality and composition of milk and is a form of adulteration.

questions.question: Which is the safest response if a suspected food sample requires chemical testing?

options.text: Use a recognised laboratory or food-safety authority

questions.explanation: Suspected adulterants should not be tasted or handled casually; testing should be done safely by appropriate facilities.

questions.question: Food adulteration can primarily result in:

options.text: Improved nutritional value in every case
Health risks and reduced food quality

questions.explanation: Adulteration may reduce nutritional quality and introduce harmful substances.

questions.question: Which information is especially useful when checking a packaged food product?
questions.explanation: Date marking and ingredient details help consumers assess packaged food safety and suitability.

questions.question: The basic structural and functional unit of life is the:
questions.explanation: The cell is the smallest unit capable of carrying out basic life processes.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is commonly called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release usable energy through cellular respiration.

questions.question: Which structure controls many activities of a typical cell and contains genetic material?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains chromosomes and regulates many cell activities.

questions.question: Which feature is generally present in plant cells but absent in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells usually have a rigid cell wall; animal cells do not.

questions.question: The basic unit of biological classification is:
questions.explanation: Species is the basic unit of classification.

questions.question: Who introduced the system of binomial nomenclature?
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus is associated with the formal system of binomial nomenclature.

questions.question: Which group contains organisms that make their own food by photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Green plants generally make food using light energy, carbon dioxide and water.

questions.question: Which of the following is an invertebrate?
questions.explanation: An earthworm lacks a backbone and is therefore an invertebrate.

questions.question: The process by which organisms with favourable inherited variations tend to leave more offspring is:
questions.explanation: Natural selection changes the frequency of inherited traits over generations.

questions.question: Fossils are important because they provide evidence about:

options.text: Past life and changes in organisms
The exact age of every living person

questions.explanation: Fossils preserve evidence of organisms that lived in the past.

questions.question: An adaptation is a feature that helps an organism:

options.text: Survive and reproduce in its environment

questions.explanation: Adaptations can improve survival and reproductive success in a particular environment.

questions.question: Evolution occurs across:
questions.explanation: Evolution is change in inherited characteristics of populations over successive generations.

questions.question: A gene is a segment of:
questions.explanation: A gene is a DNA sequence that carries hereditary information.

questions.question: The observable characteristics of an organism are called its:
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to observable traits resulting from genetic and environmental influences.

questions.question: In a simple Mendelian cross, a dominant allele is generally expressed in the:
questions.explanation: A dominant allele can determine the phenotype when one copy is present in a heterozygote.

questions.question: Which structure carries genes in the cell nucleus?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are structures made of DNA and proteins and carry genes.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood throughout the human body?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through the circulatory system.

questions.question: Gas exchange in the human lungs takes place mainly in the:
questions.explanation: Alveoli are tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged.

questions.question: Which organ removes many dissolved wastes from the blood to form urine?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood and help form urine.

questions.question: Photosynthesis in green plants mainly occurs in the:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the main sites of photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which nutrient is the body's main immediate source of energy?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are a major energy source for the body.

questions.question: Deficiency of vitamin C can cause:
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, which can include bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

questions.question: Which mineral is essential for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying pigment in red blood cells.

questions.question: A balanced diet is one that:

options.text: Provides needed nutrients in suitable amounts

questions.explanation: A balanced diet supplies energy and essential nutrients in appropriate proportions for health.

questions.question: The most effective routine measure to reduce the spread of many infections is:
questions.explanation: Handwashing removes many disease-causing organisms and helps interrupt transmission.

questions.question: Vaccination helps protect a person by:

options.text: Training the immune system to recognise a pathogen
Destroying every microbe in the environment

questions.explanation: Vaccines stimulate immune memory so the body can respond more effectively to a pathogen.

questions.question: Which practice helps prevent water-borne diseases?

options.text: Storing water in open dirty containers

questions.explanation: Safe water treatment and storage reduce exposure to pathogens that cause water-borne illness.

questions.question: Which is a non-communicable disease?
questions.explanation: Diabetes is a non-communicable condition and does not spread from person to person.

questions.question: Malaria is transmitted to humans by the bite of an infected:
questions.explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria parasites to humans.

questions.question: Dengue is commonly transmitted by:
questions.explanation: Dengue virus is mainly transmitted by infected Aedes mosquitoes.

questions.question: Tuberculosis is caused by a:
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

questions.question: Which action is important in preventing the spread of cholera?
questions.explanation: Cholera spreads mainly through contaminated food and water; safe water and sanitation are key preventive measures.

questions.question: In a food chain, green plants are usually:
questions.explanation: Green plants produce organic food using sunlight and form the producer level.

questions.question: Which gas is a major contributor to the enhanced greenhouse effect from human activities?
questions.explanation: Human emissions of carbon dioxide are a major driver of the enhanced greenhouse effect.

questions.question: The 3Rs in waste management stand for:
questions.explanation: The 3Rs encourage reducing waste, reusing materials and recycling suitable materials.

questions.question: Excessive nutrients entering a lake can cause:
questions.explanation: Nutrient enrichment can cause algal blooms and oxygen depletion, a process called eutrophication.

questions.topic: Latest Inventions in Science and Technology
questions.question: Which technology converts sunlight directly into electrical energy?
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic cells convert light energy into electrical energy.

questions.topic: Latest Inventions in Science and Technology
questions.question: A satellite used mainly to relay television and communication signals is a:
questions.explanation: Communication satellites relay signals over large geographic areas.

questions.topic: Latest Inventions in Science and Technology
questions.question: Which field focuses on machines performing tasks with programmed control and sensors?
questions.explanation: Robotics combines mechanical systems, sensors and control/programming to perform tasks.

questions.topic: Latest Inventions in Science and Technology
questions.question: Artificial intelligence systems are designed primarily to:

options.text: Perform tasks associated with human-like learning or decision processes

questions.explanation: AI refers to computer systems performing tasks such as pattern recognition, prediction or language processing.

questions.question: For a current-affairs science note, which combination is most useful to record?

options.text: Only a rumour and a photograph

questions.explanation: Recording the event, date, responsible organisation and significance makes revision verifiable and useful.

questions.question: Which source is generally most appropriate for verifying an Indian space mission announcement?
questions.explanation: ISRO's official communications are a primary source for its mission announcements.

questions.question: When revising a recent scientific award, which detail should be checked carefully?

options.text: The colour of the award envelope

questions.explanation: Award recipient and year are key factual details and should be verified from a reliable source.

questions.question: Why should current-affairs notes include the date of an invention or announcement?

options.text: To distinguish recent developments from older information

questions.explanation: Dates establish the time context and help distinguish new developments from older ones.

questions.topic: Everyday Applications of Basic Principles of Mechanics, Electricity, Magnetism, Light, Sound, Heat and Nuclear Physics
questions.question: Which type of mirror is commonly used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror provides a wider field of view and forms an erect, diminished image.

questions.question: Which law states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of mass states that total mass remains constant in a chemical reaction.

questions.question: Which part of a cell controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane regulates the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

questions.question: Which blood component helps in clotting?
questions.explanation: Platelets help form clots and reduce blood loss after injury.

questions.question: Which layer of the atmosphere contains most of the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: Most atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere, where it absorbs much harmful ultraviolet radiation.

questions.explanation: Wind is replenished naturally and is a renewable energy source.
